newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China assures Hong Kong of taxation independence.
newsitem.headline: China assures Hong Kong of taxation independence.

text.p: A senior Chinese tax official said on Friday that Beijing would allow Hong Kong to practise its own tax system "independently" after the British colony returns to Chinese rule at the end of June.

However, such independence would be under the supervision of the central government in Beijing, Xiang Huaicheng, deputy director-general of China's State Administration of Taxation, said in a speech in Singapore.
"It (Hong Kong) will have its own power of tax legislation, design its own taxes, items and rates," Xiang said in a speech on China's policies.
Hong Kong would also confer tax concessions on its own and make its own decisions on other tax affairs, Xiang said.

Beijing, which takes back Hong Kong after more than 150 years of British rule, has guaranteed the territory can function as a separate entity from the rest of China with its own political and economic system for 50 years.
"After the reunification, tax laws and regulations made in the mainland will not be applicable to Hong Kong," Xiang said.
China would allow Hong Kong to conclude and implement tax treaties and maintain or develop tax relations with other countries under the name "Hong Kong, China", he said.
Those international agreements to which China is a party would be "decided by the central government" after seeking views of the Hong Kong government, Xiang said.
As Hong Kong firms will be considered foreign companies after July, they will still enjoy tax privilages applied to foreign firms, he said.
